source_meta._title: '/locate', explorer maps, and treasure maps can cause extreme TPS lag, even leading to a complete server freeze if structure generation is turned off

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition singleplayer, using the integrated server in snapshot 18w08b. Create a fresh disposable Default world in Creative mode with commands permitted and Generate Structures disabled. No mods, datapacks, external server, other players, supplied seed, or pre-generated world are required.
preconditions: Install or enable the historical Java Edition snapshot 18w08b in the Minecraft Launcher.
Use an isolated game directory if possible so this old snapshot does not open or modify newer worlds.
Close unrelated work before testing because the report states that the trigger can make the integrated server unresponsive.
Use a new disposable test world; do not perform this test in a valued save.
Do not run the command repeatedly. One command submission is sufficient for the observation subsystem.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for Java Edition snapshot 18w08b and start the game. If creating the installation now, enable historical snapshots in the launcher's installation/version settings and assign a separate game directory before selecting 18w08b.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches its title screen and the displayed version identifies 18w08b.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World. Do not open an existing world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Enter a recognizable disposable world name, then click the Game Mode button until it shows Creative. Creative mode is an execution choice that provides command access without adding unrelated survival setup.
steps.success_cue: The world name is entered and the Game Mode button shows Creative.

steps.action: Select More World Options to open the additional world-generation settings.
steps.success_cue: The screen displays options including the seed, world type, Generate Structures, and Allow Cheats settings.

steps.action: Leave the seed field empty and leave World Type set to Default. This allows a random seed while avoiding an unrelated specialized world generator.
steps.success_cue: The seed field is empty and World Type shows Default.

steps.action: Click the Generate Structures button until its displayed value is OFF. Do not create the world while this option says ON.
steps.success_cue: The button reads Generate Structures: OFF.

steps.action: Ensure Allow Cheats is ON so the in-game /locate command can be submitted. If Creative mode has already forced this setting on, leave it on.
steps.success_cue: The button reads Allow Cheats: ON, or the interface otherwise indicates that commands are permitted.

steps.action: Select Done to return to the main Create New World screen without changing the configured options.
steps.success_cue: The main Create New World screen is visible again with the chosen world name and Creative mode retained.

steps.action: Select Create New World once. Wait for world creation and the initial loading screen to finish.
steps.success_cue: The player appears in the newly created world.

steps.action: Wait until nearby terrain has rendered and normal look and movement controls respond. Do not explore or intentionally load additional chunks before running the test.
steps.success_cue: The spawn-area terrain is visible and the player can look or move without initial world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Press T, the default Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat input. Use in-game chat rather than a server console because this is a singleplayer integrated-server reproduction.
steps.success_cue: A chat input line with a text cursor is visible at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Type the report-supplied locate command exactly as shown, including the leading slash and the capital V in Village. Do not press Enter yet.
steps.success_cue: The complete text /locate Village is visible in the chat input line with no extra characters.

steps.action: Press Enter once to submit the command. Make no further player inputs or additional command attempts after submission; immediately transfer control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The chat input has accepted the command submission, and the single /locate Village invocation has just begun processing.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in a fresh 18w08b Creative singleplayer world created with Generate Structures disabled, and /locate Village has just been submitted once through in-game chat. Begin observing integrated-server responsiveness immediately without issuing another command.
uncertainties: The report's clearest menu-by-menu structures-disabled reproduction was explicitly documented for 1.14.4. The same report-supported world condition and historical /locate Village form are applied here to the first listed affected version, Minecraft 18w08b, as required by the version-selection policy.
The report supplies no world seed. A blank seed is retained because disabling structure generation removes the need to locate a seed-dependent generated village for this reproduction path.

Minecraft 1.13-pre6 appears in both the raw Affects versions and Fix versions metadata. It was omitted from affected_versions because fix versions must not be selected as affected reproduction targets.

The duration and severity of the resulting performance interruption can vary with hardware. The plan therefore triggers the search exactly once and hands off immediately rather than requiring repeated /locate commands.

Historical snapshot menu wording can vary with language and minor UI changes. If labels differ, preserve the required state: Java Edition 18w08b, a fresh Default world, commands permitted, and structure generation disabled.
Web lookup was limited to the permitted Mojang/Minecraft domains and did not establish a more authoritative 18w08b-specific menu capture than the reproduction information supplied in the report.

source_meta._title: Clicking with an item that is out of stock in the villager trading menu with sufficient payment will allow purchase of the item regardless

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 23w07a in a single-player Creative-mode world. Creative mode is a practical setup choice for quickly obtaining a villager, workstation, and payment items; the report does not require a particular game mode or server type. Use an unmodified client and a clear area without unrelated villagers or job-site blocks. The procedure below uses a cleric selling stackable redstone dust as the concrete trade, but another villager trade with a stackable result may be used if necessary.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 23w07a, which is the only affected version listed in the report. Do not reproduce in the listed fix version, 1.19.4 Pre-release 2.
Have enough empty player-inventory space to hold all items purchased while exhausting the selected trade.
Use a villager offer whose result item is stackable. The concrete setup below attempts to use a novice cleric's redstone-dust offer.
Obtain substantially more payment than is required to exhaust the offer so that at least one additional transaction's payment remains after the red out-of-stock X appears.
Once the offer becomes out of stock, perform the remaining steps immediately and do not wait for the villager to restock.
Use the standard interaction equivalents for right-click, left-click, inventory, and shift-click if controls have been rebound.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the Java Edition installation for snapshot 23w07a, and launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 23w07a.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode. Use a fresh world and move to a clear, level area away from other villagers and job-site blocks so the test villager can claim the intended workstation.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded Creative-mode world, surrounding chunks have rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and obtain one Villager Spawn Egg, one Brewing Stand, and several stacks of Emeralds. Place the spawn egg and brewing stand in accessible hotbar slots, and keep the emeralds in the player inventory. Do not obtain redstone dust from Creative inventory; the redstone used for the cursor action should come from the villager purchases.
steps.exact_input: Press E; use the Creative inventory search to find Villager Spawn Egg, Brewing Stand, and Emerald.
steps.success_cue: The player has a Villager Spawn Egg and Brewing Stand in the hotbar, several stacks of emeralds in the inventory, and multiple empty inventory slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory, select the Villager Spawn Egg in the active hotbar slot, aim at the ground in the clear test area, and use the item once to spawn a villager.
steps.exact_input: Press E to close the inventory; select the Villager Spawn Egg; right-click the ground once.
steps.success_cue: A villager is standing in the test area.

steps.action: Confirm that the spawned villager is an adult capable of taking a profession. If it is a baby, or if it is a green-robed nitwit that cannot take a profession, spawn another villager and use the suitable adult for the following steps.
steps.success_cue: An adult, non-nitwit villager is available in the clear test area.

steps.action: Select the Brewing Stand and place it on the ground where the selected villager can walk up to and claim it as a job-site block.
steps.exact_input: Select the Brewing Stand hotbar slot and right-click the ground beside the villager.
steps.success_cue: A brewing stand is placed within the villager's reach.

steps.action: Wait for the villager to claim the brewing stand and become a cleric. Do not continue merely after a fixed delay; continue when the villager's clothing changes to the cleric profession appearance. If the villager does not claim it, confirm it is an adult non-nitwit, remove competing job-site blocks, and reposition the brewing stand within reach.
steps.success_cue: The villager has visibly changed into a cleric and can present cleric trades.

steps.action: Face the cleric and interact with it to open the villager trading menu.
steps.success_cue: The villager trading menu is open, with trade offers in the left sidebar and two payment slots plus a result slot in the main panel.

steps.action: Select a trade that sells a stackable item. For this setup, select the cleric offer that takes emerald payment and returns redstone dust. The result slot is the third trade slot: the slot to the right of the trade arrow, after the two payment slots. If this villager does not provide a stackable result offer, close the menu before making any trades and establish another suitable villager offer instead.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the sidebar entry showing emerald payment and redstone-dust output.
steps.success_cue: The selected offer displays emeralds as payment and redstone dust, a stackable item, in the result slot.

steps.action: Verify that the player has enough emeralds to buy every remaining use of the selected offer and still pay for at least one additional transaction afterward. Also verify that the inventory has room for the purchased redstone dust. If necessary, close the menu briefly and obtain additional emeralds from the Creative inventory, then reopen the same villager and reselect the same trade.
steps.success_cue: Several stacks of emeralds are available, the selected trade is ready to complete, and the player inventory has empty space for its output.

steps.action: Purchase the selected stackable item repeatedly until the villager exhausts that offer. Take each result into the player inventory; shift-left-clicking the result slot may be used to transfer purchases efficiently. Continue only until the selected offer becomes unavailable, without discarding all of the purchased output.
steps.exact_input: Repeatedly shift+left-click the redstone-dust result slot until the offer locks.
steps.success_cue: A red X is displayed over the arrow for the selected trade in the left sidebar, the main result slot is empty, and at least one stack or partial stack of redstone dust is present in the player inventory.

steps.action: Keep the trading menu open with the exhausted trade still selected. Do not switch to a different offer, close the menu, or wait for a restock.
steps.success_cue: The exhausted stackable-item offer remains selected, its red X remains visible, and its third/result slot remains empty.

steps.action: Ensure that payment for at least one more execution of the selected trade is physically present in the applicable payment input slot or slots. If enough emeralds remain there from the previous purchases, leave them in place. Otherwise, pick up emeralds from the player inventory and place at least the currently displayed price into the first payment slot, then clear the cursor before continuing.
steps.exact_input: If required: left-click an emerald stack in the inventory, then left-click the first payment input slot.
steps.success_cue: The exhausted trade remains selected, the result slot is empty, and enough emeralds for one additional transaction are visible in the trade's payment input.

steps.action: In the player-inventory portion of the still-open trading menu, find the same item that was purchased from this offer—redstone dust in this setup. Left-click its stack once, without holding Shift, so the stack is picked up and attached to the mouse cursor.
steps.exact_input: Left-click once on a redstone-dust stack in the player inventory.
steps.success_cue: A redstone-dust stack is visibly attached to the cursor, while the exhausted offer's result slot remains empty.

steps.action: Move the cursor carrying the purchased item over the empty third/result slot to the right of the trade arrow. Do not click another slot or return the carried item to the inventory.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse pointer over the empty result slot without clicking.
steps.success_cue: The cursor is directly over the empty result slot while carrying redstone dust; the selected offer still shows its red out-of-stock X and sufficient emerald payment remains present.

steps.action: With the matching purchased item still attached to the cursor and the cursor positioned over the empty result slot, left-click the result slot once, as though picking up a crafting or trading result. Make no additional input after this click.
steps.exact_input: Left-click once on the empty third/result slot.
steps.success_cue: The specified left-click has been issued under the prepared out-of-stock, sufficient-payment, matching-carried-item conditions; no subsequent inventory or trading input has occurred.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just left-clicked the exhausted trade's empty result slot while carrying the same stackable item previously purchased from that trade, with the red out-of-stock X visible and sufficient payment present. Begin observation immediately, before any further click, menu closure, villager restock, or inventory action.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a particular villager profession, offer, payment item, or result item. The cleric redstone-dust trade is a practical setup choice intended to provide a simple stackable result; another stackable-output offer may be substituted if this offer is unavailable.

The report says, 'To my knowledge, this only works on stackable items,' rather than establishing stackability as a fully tested requirement. This plan preserves that stated condition by selecting a stackable result.

The report does not state whether merely possessing sufficient payment is enough or whether payment must remain in the trading input slot. This plan uses the stronger condition by requiring sufficient payment to be physically present in the applicable input slot.

The attached video's contents were not supplied with the raw report. The cursor sequence is therefore reconstructed from the written steps as: left-click and release to pick up the purchased item, move the carried stack over the empty result slot, and then left-click that slot once.
Creative mode and single-player are not specified requirements in the report; they are selected only to make villager and payment setup deterministic and efficient.

source_meta._title: Villagers can sell experimental enchantments without the 1.21 experiment enabled

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w13a in a fresh single-player Creative world. Use a Superflat world with structures disabled as a practical way to isolate one villager from naturally generated job-site blocks. Keep both the "Update 1.21" and "Villager Trade Rebalance" experiments disabled. Use the vanilla client without custom data packs or gameplay-altering mods.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher has an installation for Java Edition snapshot 24w13a. Do not use 1.20.5 Release Candidate 2, because it is listed as the fix version rather than an affected version.
The test world must be newly created without enabling the "Update 1.21" experiment.
The "Villager Trade Rebalance" experiment must also remain disabled, based on the report's statement that the villager rework was not enabled.
Commands or cheats must be available so daytime can be held constant while repeatedly changing the villager's profession.
Use an adult, unemployed villager that has never been traded with. Completing even one trade would lock its profession and offers, preventing the required rerolls.
The report supplies no seed or fixed reroll count. Librarian offers are randomized, so the reroll loop may require an unspecified number of attempts.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation using the exact Java Edition snapshot version 24w13a, then launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is loaded and displays 24w13a as the running version.

steps.action: From the title screen, open the single-player world creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Configure the world for controlled setup: set Game Mode to Creative, set Difficulty to Peaceful, and ensure commands or cheats are allowed. The report does not require these settings; they avoid survival resource collection and hostile-mob interference.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Difficulty: Peaceful; Allow Commands/Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The world creation screen shows Creative mode, Peaceful difficulty, and commands enabled.

steps.action: In the world-generation settings, select Superflat and disable structure generation. This prevents nearby village workstations from being claimed by the test villager.
steps.exact_input: World Type: Superflat; Generate Structures: OFF
steps.success_cue: The selected world type is Superflat and structures are disabled.

steps.action: Open the Experiments settings. Leave both "Update 1.21" and "Villager Trade Rebalance" disabled, then return to the main world creation screen. Do not accept any prompt that would enable experimental features.
steps.exact_input: Update 1.21: OFF; Villager Trade Rebalance: OFF
steps.success_cue: Neither relevant experiment is enabled and the world can be created without an experimental-feature confirmation being accepted.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the newly generated world, nearby terrain is visible, and movement responds without initial loading pauses.

steps.action: Keep the world in daytime so the villager can repeatedly acquire and lose its profession. Press T to open chat, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that doDaylightCycle is false.

steps.action: Press T again, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter to set the frozen time to day.
steps.success_cue: The world is visibly in daytime and the sun no longer advances after the daylight-cycle rule was disabled.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to obtain a Villager Spawn Egg, a Lectern, a Diamond Axe, and a stack of any full solid block such as Stone. Put them into separate hotbar slots, then press E to close the inventory.
steps.exact_input: Search terms: Villager Spawn Egg; Lectern; Diamond Axe; Stone
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a villager spawn egg, a lectern, a diamond axe, and solid building blocks.

steps.action: On level ground, make a small holding cell around one empty ground square. Place solid blocks on three sides of that square, make each of those three walls two blocks high, and place a roof block above the empty square. Leave the side facing the player open at ground level so a lectern can later occupy that opening.
steps.exact_input: right-click to place each solid block
steps.success_cue: There is one empty standing space enclosed by two-block-high walls on three sides and a roof, with one side left open for the lectern.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg and right-click the floor inside the holding cell. Confirm that the spawned villager is an adult and does not already show another profession. Do not continue with a baby villager or a green-robed nitwit; create a replacement adult unemployed villager if necessary.
steps.success_cue: One adult, untraded, unemployed villager is contained in the cell.

steps.action: Select the Lectern and right-click the ground in the cell's open side, placing it directly adjacent to the villager. The lectern is the librarian job-site block, and librarians can offer enchanted books. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/de-de/article/lectern?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A lectern occupies the open side of the cell and is directly adjacent to the contained villager.

steps.action: Wait without interacting until the villager claims the lectern and changes into a librarian. Green particles may appear during the job-site change; use the librarian's profession clothing as the readiness condition.
steps.success_cue: The adult villager visibly has the librarian profession and remains next to the lectern.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so no block or spawn egg is held. Aim at the librarian and right-click once to open its trading interface. Do not complete any trade.
steps.exact_input: right-click librarian with an empty hand
steps.success_cue: The novice librarian trading interface is open and its current offers are visible.

steps.action: Inspect every displayed novice trade. For each trade whose rightmost output is an Enchanted Book, move the pointer over that output and wait for its tooltip to appear. Compare the enchantment name, regardless of level, with Density, Breach, and Wind Burst; the official 24w13a notes identify these as the three mace-exclusive enchantments. If one of those names is shown, leave the pointer over the book, do not click anything, and hand control to the observation subsystem. If none is shown, continue to step 16. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-snapshot-24w13a?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: mouse-hover over each Enchanted Book output; do not click
steps.success_cue: Either the cursor is stationary over the selected candidate book with its full tooltip visible, or every current offer has been checked without completing a trade.

steps.action: Only if the current offers contain no qualifying candidate, press Esc to close the trading interface. Do not purchase any other offer, because trading once would permanently lock this villager's current profession and trades.
steps.success_cue: The trading interface is closed, the villager remains alive, and no trade has been completed.

steps.action: Select the Diamond Axe, aim carefully at the lectern rather than the villager, and left-click to break the lectern. Breaking and replacing an untraded villager's job-site block is the reroll method for undesirable trades. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AVillager_trading_hall?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: left-click the Lectern with Diamond Axe
steps.success_cue: The lectern block is gone while the contained villager remains alive and unharmed.

steps.action: Wait until the villager releases the removed job site and visibly loses the librarian profession. Do not place the lectern again while it still appears as a librarian.
steps.success_cue: The villager has returned to its adult unemployed appearance.

steps.action: Select the Lectern and right-click the same ground position in the open side of the cell to replace it.
steps.success_cue: The lectern is again directly adjacent to the unemployed villager.

steps.action: Wait until the villager claims the replaced lectern and becomes a librarian again. This generates another set of offers because no trade has been completed.
steps.success_cue: The villager has regained the librarian profession and is ready for its newly generated offers to be opened.

steps.action: Return to step 14 and repeat the open, inspect, break, and replace cycle until step 15 reaches its handoff branch. Never complete a trade during this loop.
steps.success_cue: Each iteration begins with an untraded librarian whose newly generated trade list is ready to inspect.

stor.handoff_condition: The test remains in a 24w13a world created with both Update 1.21 and Villager Trade Rebalance disabled. A freshly rerolled librarian trading interface is open, the cursor is stationary over the candidate Enchanted Book output with its tooltip fully visible, no trade has been purchased, and the interface has not been closed. Begin observation immediately in this state.
uncertainties: The inaccessible image attachment may identify a specific enchantment and level, but the supplied text does not. The plan therefore accepts any level of Density, Breach, or Wind Burst as matching the report's generic reference to a Mace enchantment; official 24w13a notes list those three mace-exclusive enchantments. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-snapshot-24w13a?utm_source=openai))

The report gives no seed, biome, villager type, trade price, enchantment level, or number of required rerolls. The procedure must therefore repeat the randomized trade-generation loop until a qualifying candidate is generated.

Creative mode, Peaceful difficulty, Superflat generation, disabled structures, the holding cell, and frozen daytime are practical setup choices not stated as bug requirements. They are intended only to remove resource collection, wandering, hostile mobs, unrelated job sites, and work-hour timing from the reproduction.
The report lists both 24w13a and 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1 as affected. Following the required version-selection policy, this plan uses the first listed version, 24w13a.

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1 in a new single-player Creative-mode world with commands/cheats enabled. Use Normal difficulty and a flat, nonflammable outdoor test area with room for a straight line at least 23 blocks long.
preconditions: Launch exactly Java Edition 1.21.1, the first version listed as affected; do not use fix version 24w44a.
Use a new world so no entity already has the command tag mc276529_target.
The player must be in Creative mode and able to execute commands and edit command blocks.
Reserve a flat, nonflammable area large enough for a button, 20 repeaters, a command block, and a villager beside the button.
Use default controls where referenced: T opens chat, right-click performs Use Item/Place Block, and Esc closes a screen. If controls are rebound, use the corresponding bound actions.
Do not install mods, plugins, or datapacks that change villagers, trading, lightning, command blocks, or GUI behavior.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start the Java Edition 1.21.1 installation. Confirm the version displayed on the title screen before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen identifies the running game as Java Edition 1.21.1.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled and difficulty set to Normal. Enter the world and wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a responsive Creative-mode world and can use commands.

steps.action: Move to a flat, nonflammable outdoor area. Press T to open chat and execute the following /give commands one at a time, pressing Enter after each command. Keep the leading slash because these commands are being entered in in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The inventory contains at least one stone block, one stone button, 20 redstone repeaters, and one command block.

steps.action: Place the stone block at the beginning of the test circuit. Attach the stone button to an accessible face of that block. Leave a clear patch beside the button for the villager and player.
steps.success_cue: The button is attached to the stone block and can be reached while standing beside the reserved villager area.

steps.action: Starting directly against the opposite side of the button's stone block, place all 20 redstone repeaters end-to-end in one straight line. While placing them, face from the button toward the far end so every repeater passes power away from the button. Re-place any repeater facing the opposite direction.
steps.success_cue: A continuous line of exactly 20 repeaters runs away from the button block, with every repeater oriented toward the far end.

steps.action: Set every repeater to its maximum delay. Use right-click three times on each newly placed repeater, changing it from the default 1-redstone-tick setting to 4 redstone ticks. Twenty repeaters at this setting provide approximately eight seconds between pressing the button and powering the command block.
steps.exact_input: Right-click each of the 20 repeaters exactly 3 times.
steps.success_cue: All 20 repeaters are visibly set to their longest-delay configuration.

steps.action: Place the command block immediately after the output end of the twentieth repeater so that the final repeater points directly into and powers the command block.
steps.success_cue: The circuit forms one uninterrupted path: button block, 20 correctly oriented repeaters, then command block.

steps.action: Right-click the command block to open its configuration screen. Leave it as Impulse, Unconditional, and Needs Redstone. Enter the exact command below without a leading slash, then select Done.
steps.success_cue: The command block stores the lightning command and remains configured as Impulse, Unconditional, and Needs Redstone.

steps.action: Return to the button end of the circuit. Stand on level ground beside the button and face horizontally toward a clear block of ground that is not occupied by the repeater line. Press T, enter the exact summon command with its leading slash, and press Enter. The local coordinates place the villager approximately two blocks in front of the player. The command assigns the villager a farmer profession, gives it the unique target tag, and disables movement so it remains next to the activation button.
steps.success_cue: One adult farmer villager appears approximately two blocks in front of the player and remains stationary.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so the held item cannot interfere. Stand within normal interaction reach of the farmer, aim at its body, and use right-click once to perform a preflight check that it can be traded with.
steps.success_cue: A villager trading screen opens and shows the farmer's profession and at least one trade entry.

steps.action: Press Esc once to close the preflight trading screen. Do not attack, remove, replace, or summon another villager. Position the player so the button can be pressed and the same stationary farmer can then be reached immediately.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible, the tagged farmer remains beside the button, and both the button and farmer are within a few steps of the player.

steps.action: Aim at the stone button and right-click it once. This sends one pulse through the 20 maximum-delay repeaters. Do not press the button a second time.
steps.success_cue: The first repeater becomes powered and the powered state begins progressing along the repeater line toward the command block.

steps.action: Immediately turn to the same farmer, move into interaction reach if necessary, aim at its body, and right-click it before the approximately eight-second repeater delay expires.
steps.success_cue: The farmer trading screen is fully open before the delayed redstone pulse reaches the command block.

steps.action: Keep the trading screen untouched: do not press Esc, E, or another inventory key; do not click a trade; and do not move away. Wait until the delayed command executes and the lightning event occurs at the tagged villager's position. Make no further input after the lightning sound or flash.
steps.success_cue: The delayed lightning sound or flash has just occurred while the trading screen was open immediately before the strike, triggering the villager-to-witch conversion event.

stor.handoff_condition: The delayed command has just summoned lightning at the tagged villager while its trading screen was open immediately before the strike. The villager-to-witch conversion event has been triggered and the player has made no subsequent input; hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect the resulting UI state and interaction availability.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, difficulty, or single-player versus dedicated-server environment. A new Creative-mode single-player world with cheats and Normal difficulty is selected as the simplest deterministic environment.

The report does not provide exact summon or lightning commands. The plan uses version-appropriate Java command syntax, a unique entity tag, and execution at the tagged villager to prevent the lightning from targeting an unrelated entity.

The report says to give the villager a job but does not prescribe a workstation or profession. The plan assigns the farmer profession through VillagerData NBT to avoid workstation-claiming timing and randomness.

NoAI:1b is an execution aid, not a requirement stated by the report. It keeps the target beside the activation button during the timed sequence; the report does not indicate that villager movement is relevant.

The report specifies only that the command-block setup should include enough delay to open the trading GUI. Twenty repeaters at maximum delay, approximately eight seconds total, are a practical deterministic implementation.
The supplied report does not include the attachment contents, so no spatial layout from the attached video or image could be preserved.

source_meta._title: Wandering traders can sell pale oak saplings even when they're disabled

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w40a in a newly created single-player world. Use Creative mode as a practical way to obtain Wandering Trader Spawn Eggs. The world must be created with the Winter Drop experiment disabled; do not test in the listed fix version, 1.21.2 Pre-Release 1.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can start the exact Java Edition snapshot 24w40a.
Use a new world or another world known to have been created without the Winter Drop experiment enabled.
Do not enable the Winter Drop experiment at any point during world creation.
No particular seed, coordinates, biome, difficulty, emerald supply, or completed trade is required by the report.
Wandering-trader offers are randomized, so the spawn-and-inspect cycle may require an indeterminate number of attempts.

steps.action: Start Minecraft: Java Edition using the exact installation/version snapshot 24w40a. If necessary, enable snapshot installations in the Minecraft Launcher and select 24w40a before pressing Play.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running Java Edition version as 24w40a.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World to begin creating a fresh test world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Creative mode is not required by the report itself, but it provides direct access to the spawn egg explicitly allowed by the report and avoids relying on natural trader spawning.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Open the world-creation Experiments screen, normally through the More tab or the Experiments button. Locate Winter Drop and ensure its toggle is OFF. If it is already off by default, leave it unchanged. Do not enable any experiment merely to continue.
steps.success_cue: Winter Drop is displayed as disabled before world creation.

steps.action: Return to the main world-creation screen and create the world. Wait until the loading screen has closed, surrounding terrain is rendered, and normal player movement responds.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the newly created Creative-mode world, chunks around the player are rendered, and the Winter Drop experiment was not enabled during creation.

steps.action: Press the inventory control, E by default, to open the Creative inventory. Select the Search Items tab, represented by a compass if tabs are shown as icons.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open with a searchable item list visible.

steps.action: Click the Creative inventory search field and search for the Wandering Trader Spawn Egg. Place a stack of the matching spawn egg into an empty hotbar slot by clicking or using a number key while hovering over it. The hotbar is the row of nine quick-access slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: A Wandering Trader Spawn Egg is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E or Esc. Select the hotbar slot containing the Wandering Trader Spawn Egg using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E or Esc, then hotbar key 1-9 as applicable
steps.success_cue: The Wandering Trader Spawn Egg is visible in the player's hand and its name briefly appears above the hotbar.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the top surface of a nearby solid ground block with open space above it, then press the use control, right-click by default, once to spawn one wandering trader.
steps.success_cue: A new wandering trader is visible on the targeted ground near the player.

steps.action: Switch to an empty hotbar slot before interacting with the trader so that using the interact control does not spawn an additional trader accidentally.
steps.exact_input: hotbar key 1-9 for an empty slot
steps.success_cue: The player's active hand is empty and the spawned wandering trader remains nearby.

steps.action: Move close enough to the newly spawned wandering trader to target its body with the crosshair, then press the use control, right-click by default, once. Do not attack the trader and do not complete any trade.
steps.success_cue: The wandering trader trading interface is open and its list of offers is visible.

steps.action: Inspect every offer in the open trading interface. Hover the pointer over each item on the output side of the offer to display its item-name tooltip. If the complete offer list does not fit at once, use the mouse wheel or the interface scroll control to expose the remaining rows. This inspection is only for selecting the randomized trader required by the report; do not place emeralds into the trading slots or take an output item.
steps.exact_input: hover each output item; use mouse wheel or scrollbar if needed
steps.success_cue: Every offer belonging to the current trader has been exposed for tooltip identification, and no trade has been executed.

steps.action: If the current trader does not meet the report's pale-oak-sapling offer criterion, press Esc to close the trading interface, move to another clear patch of ground so traders remain distinguishable, reselect the Wandering Trader Spawn Egg, and repeat steps 9 through 12 with a newly spawned trader. Continue until the randomized criterion in the report is met. On that iteration, leave the trading interface open and do not purchase the item.
steps.success_cue: The repetition loop has stopped with the selected wandering trader's trading interface still open and no trade completed.

stor.handoff_condition: On the successful randomized iteration, the newly spawned wandering trader's trading interface has just been opened, all of that trader's offer rows are available for inspection, the Winter Drop experiment remains disabled for the world, and no trade has been executed. Hand control to the observation subsystem while leaving this interface open.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected solely to provide the spawn-egg method explicitly permitted by the report.
The report supplies no seed, coordinates, biome, difficulty, or world type, so a new default world and any clear ground near the player are used.

Wandering-trader offers are randomized, and the report gives neither the pale oak sapling offer's probability nor a maximum attempt count. The spawn-and-open loop must therefore continue for as many fresh traders as necessary.
The trigger step is step 11 on the successful loop iteration because a trader's offers become available for inspection when its trading interface is opened.
The report does not require purchasing the offer; the plan stops with the trading interface open to avoid adding an unnecessary emerald requirement.
